about: Human semantic review of the 21 concepts the render audit left REVIEW_REQUIRED (a REVIEW_REQUIRED machine verdict means no deterministic assertion covered the physics). 'decision' is the review outcome: PASS (reviewed, no defect, evidence cited), FIXED→PASS (a real defect was found and fixed, evidence cited) or REVIEW_REQUIRED (still not decidable by this repository, reason and owner decision recorded). The machine verdicts in audit-summary.json are NOT edited by this file; src/tests/physicsSemanticReview.test.ts fails if a machine REVIEW_REQUIRED concept has no entry here, or an entry cites a test that no longer exists.

phys.meas.units.initial: ST-03: text only, no drawn geometry
phys.meas.units.finding: Genuinely a text figure: a ring of the seven SI base quantities with their units, then 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². Nothing misleading is drawn; every printed pair was compared with an independently written SI table, and the newton with F = m·a.

evidence.describe: SI units figure: seven base units, and the newton built from them

phys.meas.units.remaining: None for correctness. The machine ST-03 note stays by design (no geometry to validate).

phys.meas.dimensions.initial: ST-03: text only, no drawn geometry
phys.meas.dimensions.finding: Genuinely a text figure. Every printed dimension bracket was parsed and the algebra redone: [L T⁻²][T] = [L T⁻¹] (consistent), [L T⁻²][T²] = [L] ≠ [L T⁻¹] (inconsistent), so both verdicts follow from what is printed.

evidence.describe: dimensions figure: every bracket it prints is right

phys.meas.dimensions.remaining: None for correctness. ST-03 stays by design.

phys.meas.vector-products.finding: The two panels share one pair |A|=3, |B|=4, θ=60°. Existing tests already re-derive the perpendicular, the right-hand direction of A×B and |A||B| sin θ from the drawn endpoints; this review added that the printed 6 and 10.39 are what the drawn projection and parallelogram measure.

evidence.describe: vector products: the printed 6 and 10.39 are what the drawn geometry measures
the authored figure is geometrically correct, re-derived from what it draws

phys.meas.vector-products.remaining: The A×B arrow is a fixed display length (it is an area); the narration says so.

phys.mech.free-body-diagram.initial: SM-02: no physics assertion (shared force_diagram card)
phys.mech.free-body-diagram.finding: Three real defects in the drawing: the friction arrow-head pointed AT the body (same way as the applied force — the marker was drawn pointing left and orient=auto turned it round again); applied (45) was longer than friction (40), an unbalanced body; and the body floated 20 units above the ground so the normal force had no contact.
phys.mech.free-body-diagram.fix: ForceDiagram.tsx: marker polygon along +x, one length per opposing pair, body rests on the ground line; labels lifted clear of the heads.

evidence.describe: the shared force diagram draws what each of its four concepts says

phys.mech.free-body-diagram.remaining: Forces are drawn from the body's edges, not its centre; the card draws the four standard forces only.

phys.mech.friction.initial: SM-02: no physics assertion (shared force_diagram card)
phys.mech.friction.finding: Same card: friction now points opposite the applied force, from the contact side, with the head away from the body; equal length to the applied force (static friction holding the body).

evidence.describe: the shared force diagram draws what each of its four concepts says

phys.mech.friction.remaining: The card shows the static (balanced) case; kinetic friction < applied is not drawn.

phys.mech.normal-force.initial: SM-02: no physics assertion (shared force_diagram card)
phys.mech.normal-force.finding: The body now rests on the surface, so the normal force has a contact it acts at; it is perpendicular to the surface, upward, and the same length as the weight (true for a level surface with no vertical applied force).

evidence.describe: the shared force diagram draws what each of its four concepts says

phys.mech.normal-force.remaining: Only the level-surface case is drawn: that N ≠ mg on a slope or with a vertical push is not shown and must come from the tutor's text.

phys.mech.equilibrium.initial: SM-02: no physics assertion (shared force_diagram card)
phys.mech.equilibrium.finding: The diagram was unbalanced (applied 45 vs friction 40). It now has four forces in two equal opposite pairs through the body — net force and net torque zero — which is what 'equilibrium is balanced forces, not no forces' needs.

evidence.describe: the shared force diagram draws what each of its four concepts says

phys.mech.conservation-of-momentum.initial: SM-02: no physics assertion (3D collision card)
phys.mech.conservation-of-momentum.finding: The 3D card drew unlabeled spheres and arrows: nothing said the total was the same before and after, and the sphere sizes implied masses for which the drawn velocities did not conserve momentum.
phys.mech.conservation-of-momentum.fix: visualRegistry.ts: the concept takes the 'collision' scene generator like its siblings (masses and velocities printed, elastic / perfectly inelastic switchable, total re-derived from the drawn vectors); the card stays the fallback. Recorded as a judged generator-default in visualGeneratorDefaultScope.test.ts.

evidence.describe: conservation of momentum is shown with numbers that conserve it

phys.mech.conservation-of-momentum.remaining: The totals are not printed as one number; the narration states conservation and the printed masses and velocities let the learner check it.

phys.opt.mirrors.initial: LY-02: P and F labels overlap the axis
phys.opt.mirrors.finding: P (pole) and F (focus) name points that lie ON the principal axis, so their boxes meet the axis line by construction: intentional and pedagogically correct, left where they are; their positions are verified (F at |f|, correct side for each of the four elements). Real defects found instead: the title printed magnitudes beside a signed v (1/-15 + 1/30 ≠ 1/10); the mirror was only a dot (the rays bent at nothing); and the figure used ~0.3 % of the canvas.
phys.opt.mirrors.fix: rayOptics.pure.ts: signed u, f, v in the title; the mirror plane is drawn; the camera is framed to the drawn extent.

evidence.describe: ray-optics figures print u, f and v that satisfy

phys.opt.mirrors.remaining: The mirror is drawn as a plane through the pole (paraxial convention), not as a curved surface. LY-02 stays as a machine REVIEW.

phys.opt.lenses.initial: ST-03 text only, LY-02: P / F overlap the axis
phys.opt.lenses.finding: Not text-only: the ray diagram was drawn at ~0.26 % ink with no lens. Also the lens's centre was labelled P, which is a mirror's pole (a lens has an optical centre, O), and the title printed unsigned u and f beside a signed v. F and O sit on the axis by construction (kept).
phys.opt.lenses.fix: rayOptics.pure.ts: O for lenses, signed title, the lens plane drawn, camera framed to the drawn extent.

evidence.describe: ray-optics figures print u, f and v that satisfy

phys.opt.lenses.remaining: LY-02 stays as a machine REVIEW (point labels on a line).

phys.opt.lens-power.initial: ST-03 text only, LY-02: P / F overlap the axis
phys.opt.lens-power.reason: The served figure is a correct single-lens ray diagram (the same one as phys.opt.lenses, now with O, signed numbers and the lens drawn), but the concept's two claims — power P = 1/f in dioptres and P = P₁ + P₂ for lenses in contact — are not depicted at all. scope.ts has recorded this since before this review ('one lens; P = P1 + P2 needs a combination'). Closing it means authoring a new figure from the Educational Brain's worked numbers (+5 D & −2 D → +3 D), which is new content, not a fix to what is drawn.
phys.opt.lens-power.ownerDecision: Author a lens-power / combination figure, or accept the single-lens figure as an adjacent illustration.
phys.opt.lens-power.fix: The shared lens fixes above apply (the 'P' that could read as power is now 'O').

evidence.describe: ray-optics figures print u, f and v that satisfy

phys.opt.lens-power.remaining: Stays REVIEW_REQUIRED until the owner decides.
phys.opt.lens-power.finding: Everything the figure draws is correct (the printed u, f, v satisfy 1/f = 1/v − 1/u; rays pass through F and the image), but it is the same single-lens diagram as phys.opt.lenses: it shows no power in dioptres and no combination of lenses.

phys.mod.wave-particle-duality.finding: The slits were unequal (6 and 12 units wide), the screen pattern was five hand-placed bands that were not symmetric about the axis, and a card captioned 'particles passing through two slits' showed no particles.
phys.mod.wave-particle-duality.fix: DoubleSlit.tsx: two equal slits from one geometry table; step 5 draws 150 detection dots drawn from the wave's two-slit intensity (fixed seed), captioned 'one dot = one detection' / 'wave sets where dots land'. The caption is deliberately neutral because the same card serves Young's experiment.

evidence.describe: double-slit card: two equal slits, and particles that build up a pattern

phys.mod.wave-particle-duality.remaining: Wavefronts in step 3 are schematic arcs.

phys.qm.wave-function.finding: |ψ|² is exactly ψ² (computed from ψ) and is never negative; but the y-axis arrow-head pointed left and the axis was labelled 'ψ' only although both curves are drawn on it.
phys.qm.wave-function.fix: WaveFunctionPlot.tsx: arrow marker along +x, axis labelled 'ψ, |ψ|²', the curves exported as numbers.

evidence.describe: wave-function card: |ψ|² is ψ squared, and the two are kept apart

phys.qm.wave-function.remaining: ψ is real here; a complex ψ (phase) is not drawn.

phys.qm.particle-in-box.initial: LY-02: caption overlap, SM-02: no physics assertion (potential_well card)
phys.qm.particle-in-box.finding: The levels were drawn compressed (heights 1 : 2.75 : 5) while labelled E₂ = 4E₁ and E₃ = 9E₁, so the picture contradicted its own labels. The waves were already ψₙ = sin(nπx/L), zero at both walls.
phys.qm.particle-in-box.fix: PotentialWell.tsx: level n drawn n² units above the floor.

evidence.describe: potential-well card: levels at n², and genuine particle-in-a-box states

phys.qm.hydrogen-atom-qm.initial: SM-02: no physics assertion (3D orbital card)
phys.qm.hydrogen-atom-qm.finding: The cloud shapes are the orbitals they name (1s spherical, 2s with a radial node, 2p with a nodal plane and two lobes) and are drawn as probability clouds, not orbits. The final side-by-side view showed three coloured clouds with nothing naming them (meaning by colour alone).
phys.qm.hydrogen-atom-qm.fix: HydrogenOrbital3D.tsx: 1s / 2s / 2p labels through the shared SceneLabelLayer (auto-rotation off, as for every labelled 3D card).

evidence.describe: hydrogen orbital card: the cloud shapes are the orbitals they name

phys.qm.hydrogen-atom-qm.remaining: Quantum numbers and energy levels are not drawn; the three clouds are not to a common scale.

phys.qm.spin.finding: One beam in, split into exactly two symmetric outcomes labelled +½ and −½; the caption says spin is quantised and never calls it a rotation.

evidence.describe: Stern–Gerlach card: one beam in, two symmetric outcomes

phys.qm.quantum-tunneling.finding: Inside the barrier the curve was decay × cos(…), i.e. still oscillating, where ψ must be a real exponential decay (evanescent); and the transmitted wave started at 4× the amplitude the decay had reached at the barrier's far wall, so the figure did not join up there.
phys.qm.quantum-tunneling.fix: QuantumTunneling.tsx: a real exponential from the incident amplitude, the transmitted wave starting at exactly the decayed amplitude (amp·e^(−κ)) with the incident wavelength (energy unchanged); the incident label moved above the crests.

evidence.describe: quantum tunneling card draws an evanescent barrier region

phys.qm.quantum-tunneling.remaining: Reflection from the barrier is not drawn.

phys.astro.gravitational-waves.finding: An ordered pathway (accelerating masses → ripples in spacetime → amplitude falls as 1/r → interferometer measures strain), in the Educational Brain's order. It says no medium is needed, says 1/r not 1/r², and defines strain h = ΔL/L; it draws no medium and no claim contradicts the entry.

evidence.describe: gravitational-waves figure: the stages are in physical order

phys.particle.particle-classification.finding: The tree was scrambled by the label solver at 390 px and 1280 px ('leptons' above 'particles', 'hadrons' below its own children) because two 20-character labels were 4.8 units apart.
phys.particle.particle-classification.fix: physicsCoreScenesB10.ts: the tree is data (PARTICLE_TREE), names short with qualifiers on a second line, spaced so no label leaves its place; examples (p, n / π, K) moved into the narration to stay inside the nine-label budget.

evidence.describe: conservation-laws figure: the printed tallies and verdicts are the ones the particles give
